body.statement: For every fixed \(K\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), the independent allocation in \(\mathrm{def:independent\text{-}qstar\text{-}design}\) and the total estimator \(\delta_n^\star\) satisfy \[\sup_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n^\star,\delta_n^\star;y)\le n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Equivalently, \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)\ge\Lambda_c\).
body.justification: This constructs the contrast-specific nonlinear procedure that realizes the proposed coefficient.
body.gap: The fixed-allocation multi-arm expansion does not establish that no dependent design has a larger second-order improvement.
body.consumer: A prospective four-regimen trial obtains an explicit contrast-weighted allocation and full-label shrinkage rule.
body.proof_tex:
For a schedule \(y\), put \(t_i=(Y_i(a))_{a\in S_c}\), \(\theta_i=c^\top t_i\), and \(u_i=(g^\star)^\top b_{t_i}\).  The target is \(\tau_c(y)=n^{-1}\sum_i\theta_i\), because \(c^\top\mathbf 1=0\).  Under \(q^\star_a=|c_a|/2\), the score identities are
\[
\mathbb E T_i=\theta_i,\qquad \mathbb E U_i=u_i,
\]
\[
\mathbb E T_i^2=\sum_{a\in S_c}\frac{c_a^2}{4q_a^\star}=1,
\qquad
\mathbb E(T_iU_i)=\sum_{a\in S_c}\frac{c_ag_a^\star}{4q_a^\star}
=(g^\star)^\top v=1.
\]
The dual constraints and \((\ell^\star)^\top v=\kappa(c)\) give
\[
|u_i|\le \theta_i^2/\kappa(c).
\tag{1}
\]
All random variables in these displays are bounded by constants depending only on the fixed contrast.

We next record the scaling of the Airy feedback.  The Riccati identity in the cited unit-scale Airy result implies \(-4\psi''+|x|\psi=C_A\psi\).  For every compactly supported smooth \(f\), integration by parts gives the ground-state identity
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|f'|^2+(|x|-C_A)f^2\}\,dx
=4\int_{\mathbb R}\psi^2\left|\left(\frac f\psi\right)'\right|^2\,dx\ge0.
\]
Approximation extends it to the variational domain, while equality holds at \(\psi\); thus \(\psi\) is the unit-scale minimizer specified by the definition of \(C_A\).  A change of variables in that variational problem now gives
\[
\phi_\kappa(x)=\kappa(c)^{1/6}\psi(\kappa(c)^{1/3}x),
\qquad
h_\kappa(x)=\kappa(c)^{1/3}h(\kappa(c)^{1/3}x).
\]
Consequently
\[
h_\kappa(x)^2-2h_\kappa'(x)=\kappa(c)|x|-C_A\kappa(c)^{2/3}
=\kappa(c)|x|-\Lambda_c.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, for a finite \(M_c\),
\[
|h_\kappa'(x)|\le \frac{M_c}{1+\sqrt{|x|}},
\tag{3}
\]
and \(h_\kappa^2\) and \(h_\kappa'\) are globally Lipschitz.  These conclusions use only the displayed scaling and the cited unit-scale bounds.

Set
\[
X_i=T_i-\theta_i,\quad W_i=U_i-u_i,\quad
A_n=\sum_iX_i,\quad x_n=n^{-2/3}\sum_i u_i,\quad
S_n=n^{-2/3}\sum_iU_i.
\]
Independence is a primitive of \(\mathcal D_n^\star\).  Thus
\[
\mathbb E A_n^2=\sum_i(1-\theta_i^2).
\tag{4}
\]
For each \(i\), put \(S_{-i}=x_n+n^{-2/3}\sum_{j\ne i}W_j\).  Taylor's formula at \(S_{-i}\), the Lipschitz property of \(h_\kappa'\), and independence give
\[
\mathbb E\{X_i h_\kappa(S_n)\}
=n^{-2/3}(1-\theta_i u_i)\mathbb E h_\kappa'(S_{-i})+O_c(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Since \(\mathbb E|S_{-i}-x_n|\le C_c n^{-1/6}\), the Lipschitz property again yields, uniformly in the schedule,
\[
\mathbb E\{A_n h_\kappa(S_n)\}
=n^{1/3}h_\kappa'(x_n)-n^{-2/3}h_\kappa'(x_n)\sum_i\theta_i u_i
+O_c(n^{1/6}).
\tag{5}
\]
Likewise, global Lipschitz continuity of \(h_\kappa^2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E h_\kappa(S_n)^2=h_\kappa(x_n)^2+O_c(n^{-1/6}).
\tag{6}
\]

Before projection, the squared-error risk is, by (4)--(6),
\[
\frac1n-\frac1{n^2}\sum_i\theta_i^2
+n^{-4/3}\{h_\kappa(x_n)^2-2h_\kappa'(x_n)\}
+2n^{-7/3}h_\kappa'(x_n)\sum_i\theta_i u_i+O_c(n^{-3/2}).
\tag{7}
\]
To control the penultimate term without losing uniformity when \(|x_n|\) grows, use (1) and (3):
\[
\left|2n^{-7/3}h_\kappa'(x_n)\sum_i\theta_i u_i\right|
\le \frac{C_c n^{-7/3}}{1+\sqrt{|x_n|}}\sum_i\theta_i^2.
\]
Also, (1) implies
\[
\sum_i\theta_i^2\ge\kappa(c)\left|\sum_i u_i\right|
=\kappa(c)n^{2/3}|x_n|.
\tag{8}
\]
Combining the last two displays with the negative variance term in (7), and using \(|x_n|\le C_c n^{1/3}\), gives
\[
-n^{-2}\sum_i\theta_i^2
+2n^{-7/3}h_\kappa'(x_n)\sum_i\theta_i u_i
\le-\kappa(c)|x_n|n^{-4/3}+O_c(n^{-3/2}).
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, the possible loss after applying (8) is at most
\(C_cn^{-5/3}|x_n|/(1+\sqrt{|x_n|})=O_c(n^{-3/2})\).

Substitution of (2) and (9) into (7) proves
\[
\sup_y\mathbb E\left[\left\{n^{-1}\sum_iT_i-n^{-2/3}h_\kappa(S_n)-\tau_c(y)\right\}^2\right]
\le \frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+O_c(n^{-3/2}).
\]
The target lies in \([-1,1]\), so metric projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared error.  This is precisely the asserted bound for \(\delta_n^\star\).  Finally, the definition of the minimax game gives \(R_n(c)\le\sup_y\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n^\star,\delta_n^\star;y)\), which is equivalent to the stated lower limit for \(n^{4/3}d_n(c)\).
